description: Open source observability platform for logs, metrics, traces, RUM (web, android, ios), Session replay, pipelines, SLO and LLM observability. A sophisticated, simple and highly performant alternative to Datadog, Splunk, and Elasticsearch with 140x lower storage costs and single binary deployment.

sources.entry: OpenObserve | Observability platform for logs, metrics and traces

summary.one_liner: OpenObserve is a self-hostable, single-binary observability platform for logs, metrics, traces, RUM, session replay, pipelines, and LLM observability, positioned as an alternative to Datadog, Splunk, and Elasticsearch.
summary.what_it_does: The platform ingests logs, metrics, and traces (built on OpenTelemetry) and lets users search them with SQL, and metrics with SQL or PromQL. It includes a web UI with full-text log search, distributed tracing views (waterfalls, flame graphs, Gantt charts), a service graph, and dashboards with 19+ chart types and a drag-and-drop builder. It also offers alerts with anomaly detection, incident grouping, and a visual pipeline editor that enriches, redacts, or converts data at ingest time, including logs-to-metrics. Frontend monitoring (Core Web Vitals, error tracking, session replay) and AI/LLM observability are listed as features. The README says data is stored in Parquet columnar format on S3-compatible object storage, and claims up to 140x lower storage cost than Elasticsearch.
use_cases: real user monitoring and session replay
log-to-metrics pipelines and data redaction at ingest
how_to_run: Open http://localhost:5080 and log in with the root credentials set above
For other install methods, see the quickstart documentation in the project docs
For clustered deployments, see the High Availability deployment guide
notable: Single binary deployment, with a Docker quickstart that runs in one command
Parquet columnar storage on S3-native design, claimed 140x lower storage cost
Queries logs and traces with SQL and metrics with SQL or PromQL
Visual pipeline editor using VRL for ingest-time transforms
Open source edition is AGPL-3.0; Enterprise edition is under a separate commercial license
caveats: Enterprise-only features include SSO (SAML, LDAP/AD), advanced RBAC, audit trails, federated search, and sensitive data redaction
All ingested data is immutable; only whole retention periods can be dropped
Cloud free tier is limited to 50 GB/day of ingestion, with registration required at that level
Performance and cost claims (140x storage, quarter of hardware) are the project's own statements in the README
